key_insight: PC-GNO learns the full mid-plane six-component stress tensor field in concrete penetration by coupling graph neural operator message passing to physics-informed interface interactions.
engineering_relevance: It enables field-level surrogate prediction from known design inputs, supporting faster evaluation of penetration resistance, strength criteria, and energy indicators without resolving every aggregate.
method: Aggregate-resolved FE simulations generate 359 training cases across 100, 135, and 165 m/s impacts and 14, 23, and 48 MPa concrete strengths.
Graph message-passing strength is built from impedance contrast across material interfaces.
Spectral normalization constrains updates for stable field evolution prediction.
evidence_signal: The model was validated on laboratory-backed data and reached 80.16% mean accuracy in the single-step setting, outperforming both a strong Fourier neural operator baseline and linear regression.
watch_item: Applicability is limited to the training/evaluation domain, so extrapolation to unseen concrete mixtures, geometries, or impact regimes should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: A physics-coupled graph neural operator for mid-plane six-component stress tensor field prediction in concrete penetration
